packageRules.description: Supply-chain inputs (actions, container images) are always human-reviewed; label them for triage.
Org practice: automerge patch-level Go module updates once every check passes. platformAutomerge=false makes Renovate itself wait for all checks, independent of repo auto-merge settings.
Let new module and action releases age before proposing them, so a compromised or yanked release is usually caught upstream first. Docker registries without timestamps are excluded.
Actions are pinned to full-semver tags, so a digest-only change means the tag was moved (the tj-actions pattern). Never a routine PR: require explicit approval on the dependency dashboard.

Cluster API and the Kubernetes client libraries move together: sigs.k8s.io/cluster-api vN is built against one k8s.io/* minor and one controller-runtime minor, and mixing them breaks the v1beta2 contract. The k8s.io staging modules (api, apimachinery, client-go, cluster-bootstrap, ...) are released in lockstep, so every one this module requires directly belongs here. Their minor and major bumps are grouped and held for approval so each is reviewed as the single decision it is; patch releases stay on the patch automerge rule above.

go.mod's go directive is the minimum Go the module requires, and its ceiling is set by the tooling that has to parse the module, not by what Go has released. Hold it for explicit approval. It stays out of the Go toolchain group below: Renovate holds a whole branch when any update in it needs approval, so a held directive bump would also hold the CI and builder bumps.

The Go that CI tests with (the go-version input of actions/setup-go, in ci.yaml and release.yaml) and the Go the image is built with (the golang builder image in the Dockerfile) are one decision: CI should test the Go that ships. Group them on one branch. Matched by manager, dep type and name rather than datasource, because Renovate has changed the datasource it uses for setup-go. The builder may run ahead of the go directive; builder >= directive is the invariant, not equality.
